translations.text: The words of Amos, who was among the sheep breeders of Tekoa, which he saw concerning the people of Israel in the days of Uzziah king of Judah and in the days of Jeroboam son of Joash, king of Israel, two years before the earthquake.
He said: The Lord will roar from Zion and raise his voice from Jerusalem. The shepherds’ encampments will sit in mourning, and the summit of Carmel will dry up.
This is what the Lord says: For three sins of Damascus, and for four, I will not relent toward them, because they threshed Gilead with iron threshing blades.
I will send fire upon the house of Hazael, and it will consume the fortresses of Ben-hadad.
I will break the bars of Damascus and destroy the inhabitants of the Valley of Aven and the one who holds the scepter in Beth-eden. The people of Aram will be taken captive to Kir, says the Lord.
This is what the Lord says: For three sins of Gaza, and for four, I will not relent toward them, because they took an entire population captive to hand them over to Edom.
I will send fire upon the walls of Gaza, and it will consume its fortresses.
I will destroy the inhabitants of Ashdod and the one who holds the scepter in Ashkelon. I will turn my hand against Ekron, and the remaining Philistines will perish, says the Lord of lords.

This is what the Lord says: For three sins of Tyre, and for four, I will not relent toward them, because they handed an entire population of captives over to Edom and did not remember the covenant of brotherhood.
I will send fire upon the walls of Tyre, and it will consume its fortresses.

This is what the Lord says: For three sins of Edom, and for four, I will not relent toward them, because he pursued his brother with the sword and stifled his compassion. He maintained his anger forever and kept his resentment for all time.
I will send fire upon Teman, and it will consume the fortresses of Bozrah.
This is what the Lord says: For three sins of the Ammonites, and for four, I will not relent toward them, because they ripped open the pregnant women of Gilead to enlarge their territory.
I will set fire to the streets of Rabbah, and it will consume its citadel, amid shouting on the day of battle, amid a whirlwind on the day of the storm.
Milcom will go into captivity, together with his priests and his officials, says the Lord.
This is what the Lord says: For three sins of Moab, and for four, I will not relent toward them, because they burned the bones of the king of Edom into lime.
I will send fire upon Moab, and it will consume the citadels of Kerioth. Moab will die amid turmoil, amid shouting and the sound of the trumpet.
I will destroy the judge from its midst and kill all its officials with him, says the Lord.

This is what the Lord says: For three sins of Judah, and for four, I will not relent toward them, because they rejected the law of the Lord and did not keep his commandments. Their worthless idols, which their ancestors followed, led them astray.
I will send fire upon Judah, and it will consume the fortresses of Jerusalem.
This is what the Lord says: For three sins of Israel, and for four, I will not relent toward them, because they sold the righteous for silver and the poor for a pair of sandals.
They trample on the dust of the earth and crush the poor, and they twist the path of the afflicted. A man and his father go to the same woman, defiling my holy name.
They wrapped themselves in garments taken as pledges beside every altar, and they drank aged wine in the house of their gods.
Yet I destroyed the Amorite before them, whose height was like the height of a cedar and who was strong as an oak. I destroyed his fruit above and his roots below.
I brought you up from the land of Egypt and led you through the wilderness for forty years. I brought you to this place to possess the land of the Amorites.
I raised up prophets from among your sons and Nazirites from among your young men. Is this not so, people of Israel? says the Lord.
But you gave the Nazirites wine to drink and commanded the prophets not to prophesy.
Look, I am weighed down beneath you, as a cart full of sheaves is weighed down.
The swift will lose their speed, the strong will not maintain their strength, and the warrior will not save his life.
The archer will not stand his ground, the swift runner will not escape, and the horseman will not save his life.
Even someone whose heart is as strong as a warrior’s will flee naked on that day, says the Lord.
Hear this word that the Lord has spoken against you, people of Israel, against the whole family that I brought up from the land of Egypt. I said:
You alone have I known among all the peoples and all the families of the earth. Therefore I will punish you for all your sins.
Do two people walk together unless they have agreed to meet?
Does a lion roar in the forest when it has no prey? Does a lion raise its voice from its den unless it has made a kill?
Does a bird fall into a trap on the ground without a hunter? Or does a trap spring up from the ground and catch something?
Is a trumpet sounded in a city without the people trembling? Does disaster happen in a city unless the Lord has brought it about?
For the Lord of lords does nothing unless he reveals his secret to his servants the prophets.
The lion has roared; who will not be afraid? The Lord of lords has spoken; who will not prophesy?
Proclaim on the citadels of Ashdod and on the citadels of the land of Egypt, and say: Gather, all of you, on the mountain of Samaria, and see the great turmoil within it and the oppression there.
They do not know how to do what is right, says the Lord, and they store up plunder and loot in their fortresses.
For this is what the Lord says: Distress will surround the land, its strength will be brought down, and its citadels will be plundered.

This is what the Lord says: Just as a shepherd rescues two legs or a piece of an ear from a lion’s mouth, so the Israelites who live in Samaria will be rescued, with a sudden rod and with the people from Damascus.
Hear and testify against the house of Jacob, says the mighty Lord of lords, the God of Israel.
For on the day when I punish Israel for its wrongdoing, I will also punish the altars of Bethel. The horns of the altars will be cut off and fall to the ground.
I will destroy the winter house along with the summer house. The ivory houses will perish, and many houses will come to an end, says the Lord.
Hear this word, you cows of Bashan on the mountain of Samaria, who oppress the poor and torment the needy, who say to their masters, ‘Bring us something to drink!’
The Lord of lords has sworn by his holiness: Look, days are coming upon you when they will carry you away with weapons, and those of you who remain with fishermen’s hooks.
Each woman will run toward the breach straight ahead of her, and you will be thrown onto the mountain of Armenia, says the Lord.
Go into Bethel and sin! Multiply your sins at Gilgal! Bring your sacrifices in the morning and your tithes every three days.
Offer a thanksgiving sacrifice made with leavened bread, make vows, and fulfill them, for this is what you love, Israelites, says the Lord.
I also gave you dull teeth in all your cities and a shortage of bread in all your settlements. Yet you did not return to me, says the Lord.
I also withheld rain from you three months before harvest. I sent rain down on one city but not on another. Rain would fall on one field, while a plot on which no rain fell would dry up.
Two or three cities would gather at one city to drink water, but they would not have enough. Yet you did not return to me, says the Lord.
I struck you with scorching heat, mildew, and hail. The locust devoured the abundance of your gardens, vineyards, fig trees, and olive trees. Yet you did not return to me, says the Lord.

I sent a plague among you as I did in Egypt. I killed your young men with the sword, while your horses were taken captive. I brought the stench of your rotting bodies into your faces. Yet you did not return to me, says the Lord.
I brought destruction among you as God destroyed Sodom and Gomorrah. You became like a burning stick rescued from the flames. Yet you did not return to me, says the Lord.
Therefore this is what I will do to you in the end, Israel. Because I am doing this to you, prepare, Israel, to call upon your God.

For the one who created the winds and created the mountains, who makes known to human beings what his praise is, who makes the dawn dark and treads upon the heights of the earth—the Lord, the mighty God, is his name.
Hear this word that I take up as a lament over you, house of Israel:
Virgin Israel has fallen and will not rise again. She lies abandoned on the ground, with no one to raise her.
For this is what the Lord of lords says: A city from which a thousand went out will have a hundred left, and one from which a hundred went out will have ten left for the house of Israel.
For this is what the Lord says to the house of Israel: Seek me and live.
Do not seek Bethel, do not enter Gilgal, and do not cross over to Beersheba. For Gilgal will certainly go into captivity, and Bethel will become as though it had never existed.
Seek the Lord and live, so that he does not burn like fire in the house of Joseph and consume Bethel, with no one to put it out.
You turn justice into bitterness and cast righteousness to the ground.

The one who made the Pleiades and Arcturus, who turns the shadows of death into morning and darkens day into night, who calls for the waters of the sea and pours them over the face of the earth—the Lord is his name.
He gives the weak power over the strong and raises the lowly above the exalted.
They hate the poor at the gate and despise anyone who speaks honestly.

Therefore, because you have beaten down the poor and taken choice gifts from them, you will not live in the houses of cut stone that you have built, and you will not drink the wine of the desirable vineyards that you have planted.
For I know that your offenses are many and your sins are grave. You oppressors of the righteous have taken bribes and turned the poor aside at the city gate.
Therefore, anyone with understanding will remain silent at that time, because it is an evil time.
Seek good and not evil, so that you may live. Then the mighty Lord will be with you, as you have said.
Hate evil, love good, and establish justice at the city gate. Perhaps the Lord, the mighty God, will have mercy on the remnant of Joseph.

For this is what the Lord, the mighty God, says: In all the marketplaces there will be mourning women, and in all the open places people will say, ‘Alas! Alas!’ They will call the farmers to mourning, along with the mourning women and those skilled in lamentation.
There will be wailing in all the vineyards, because I am passing through your midst, says the Lord.
Woe to those who long for the day of the Lord! What will the day of the Lord mean for you? It is darkness and not light.
It is like a man who flees from a lion and encounters a bear, or enters a house, rests his hand against the wall, and is bitten by a snake.
That is what the day of the Lord is like: it is darkness and not light, gloom without any brightness.
I hate and reject your festivals, and I will not smell the fragrance at your solemn assemblies.
Even if you offer me whole burnt offerings, I will not be pleased with your offerings, nor will I look upon the fine appearance of your fattened animals.
Take the sound of your songs away from me; I will no longer listen to the music of your harp.
Let justice come forth like water, and righteousness like a mighty stream.
Did you offer me sacrifices and offerings for forty years in the wilderness, house of Israel?
Instead, you carried the tent of Milcom and Chiun your image, the star that you made into a god for yourselves.
I will send you into exile beyond Damascus, says the Lord, whose name is God Almighty.
Woe to those who despise Zion and trust in the mountain of Samaria, who appoint the leaders of the nations, and to whom the Israelites have gone into exile!
Cross over to Calneh and see. Go from there to Hamath the Great, and go down to Gath of the Philistines. Is it better than all these kingdoms? Is their territory larger than yours?
You who await the evil day and usher in the reign of violence,
They lie on ivory beds and lounge on their couches, eating fattened lambs from the flock and calves from among the cattle.
who strum harps and, like David, devise musical instruments for themselves,
who drink clear wine and anoint themselves with the finest oils, but are not concerned about Joseph’s ruin—
therefore they will be the first to go into exile, and joy will be taken away from their rulers.
The Lord of lords has sworn by himself, and the Lord, the mighty God, has said, “I despise Jacob’s glory and hate his palaces. I will hand over the city and everything in it.”
If ten men remain in one house, they will die.

His uncle or a close relative will carry him away to bring the bones out of the house. He will say to the one who is in the house, “Is anyone else with you in the house?” He will answer him, “No,” because they have perished for not calling on the name of the Lord.
For look, the Lord will go out and strike the great house and shake it, and strike the small house and lay it waste.
Do horses run on rock, or does anyone draw a plow with them? Yet you have turned justice into bitterness and the fruit of righteousness into wormwood.
You rejoice over nothing and say, “Have we not taken a city for ourselves by our own strength?”
“For look, I am raising up a nation against you, house of Israel,” says the Lord, the mighty God. “They will oppress you from the entrance to Hamath as far as the ravine of the Arabah.”
This is what the Lord of lords showed me: the forming of locusts when the late crop was beginning to sprout. That late crop came after the king’s mowing.
When it had finished eating the vegetation of the land, I said, “Lord of lords, have mercy on me! Who will raise Jacob up? He is so small!”
The Lord relented concerning this, and it would not happen.
This is what the Lord of lords showed me: the Lord of lords was calling for judgment by fire. It consumed the great deep and consumed the allotted portion.
I said, “Lord of lords, spare me! Who will raise Jacob up? For he is small.”
The Lord reversed this, and this too will not happen.
This is what he showed me: Look, the Lord was standing on a wall of adamant, with adamant in his hand.
The Lord said to me, “What do you see, Amos?” I said, “Adamant.” The Lord said to me, “Look, I am placing adamant among my people Israel. I will no longer pass over them.”
The shrines of mockery will be devastated, and the sanctuaries of Israel will be destroyed. I will rise against the house of Jeroboam with the sword.
Amaziah, the priest of Bethel, sent word to Jeroboam king of Israel, saying, “Amos has rebelled against you within the house of Israel. The land cannot endure his words.”
For this is what Amos says: ‘Jeroboam will be killed by the sword, and Israel will be taken captive from its land.’”
Amaziah said to Amos, “Seer, flee! Go away to the land of Judah. Eat your bread there, and prophesy there.”
But do not prophesy at Bethel anymore, because it is the king’s sanctuary and a royal residence.”
Amos answered Amaziah, “I was not a prophet, nor was I a prophet’s son. Rather, I am a shepherd and a gatherer of sycamore figs.”
The Lord took me from following the flock, and the Lord said to me, “Go, prophesy against my people Israel.”
“Now hear the word of the Lord. You said, ‘Do not prophesy against the house of Israel, and do not teach the house of Isaac.’”

“Therefore this is what the Lord says: ‘Your wife will become a prostitute in your city. Your sons and daughters will fall by the sword. Your land will be divided with a measuring line. You yourself will die in an unclean land, and Israel will be taken captive from its land.’”
This is what the Lord of lords showed me: there was a sign of the end.
The Lord said to me, “What do you see, Amos?” I said, “A sign of the end.” The Lord said to me, “The end has come upon my people Israel. I will no longer turn it away from them.”
“The temple’s songs of praise will cease on that day. On that very day,” says the Lord of lords, “corpses will multiply everywhere and be thrown out for destruction.”
Hear this, you who despise the poor and do away with the needy of the land,

They say, “When will the new moon be over so that we can sell grain, and the Sabbath be over so that we can open the storehouses, make the measures smaller, make the weights heavier, and use dishonest scales?”
Then we can buy the poor for silver and the needy in exchange for [?], and sell the sweepings of the storehouses.”
The Lord, the Mighty One of Jacob, has sworn: “I will never forget any of their deeds.”
Will the earth not tremble because of these things, and all its inhabitants sit in mourning? Its edge will rise like a river; it will surge and subside like the river of Egypt.
“On that day,” says the Lord, “I will make the sun set at noon and darken the earth in broad daylight.

I will turn your festivals into mourning and all your songs into laments. I will fasten sackcloth around all your waists and bring baldness upon all your heads. I will make it like mourning for an only child, and its end like a bitter day.
“Look, the days are coming,” says the Lord, “when I will send a famine in the land—not hunger for bread or thirst for water, but for hearing the word of the Lord.”
They will gather from sea to sea and from north to east. They will hurry about seeking the word of the Lord, but they will not find it.
On that day the beautiful young women and the young men will faint from thirst.
Those who used to swear by the idols of Samaria and say, “As your god lives, Dan,” and, “As the way of Beersheba lives,” will fall and will not rise.

I saw the Lord standing over the altar. He said, “Strike the pillar’s capital so that the thresholds shake, and break them over everyone’s heads. I will kill the rest of them with the sword. Not one of them who flees will escape, and not one of them who gets away will be saved.”
If they go down to Sheol, my hand will bring them up from there. If they ascend to heaven, I will bring them down from there.
“If they hide on the summit of Carmel, I will search them out and take them from there. If they hide from my sight in the depths of the sea, I will command the serpent there to bite them.”
And if they go into captivity before their enemies, there I will command the sword to kill them. I will set my eyes on them for harm and not for good.
The mighty Lord of lords says, he who touches the earth and it shakes, and all its inhabitants sit in mourning: its edge rises like a river and sinks like the river of Egypt.
He builds his stairways in heaven, and his dominion is established on earth. He calls for the waters of the sea and pours them over the surface of the earth. The mighty Lord is his name.
Look, you are like the Cushites to me, people of Israel, says the Lord. Did I not bring Israel up from the land of Egypt, the Philistines from Cappadocia, and Aram from Kir?
Look, the eyes of the Lord of lords are on the sinful kingdom, and I will destroy it from the face of the earth. Yet I will not destroy the house of Jacob in this way, says the Lord.
For look, I am giving the command, and I will scatter the house of Israel among all the nations, as things are sifted in a sieve, and not even their smallest grain will fall to the ground.
All the sinners of my people will fall by the sword, those who say, “Disaster will not come near us or reach us.”
On that day I will raise up David’s fallen tent. I will close their breaches and raise up their ruins, and I will rebuild it as in the days of old and as in the years of past generations.
So that they may possess the remnant of Edom and all the nations over whom my name has been called, says the Lord, who does these things.

Look, the days are coming, says the Lord, when threshing will overtake harvesting, and the pressing of grapes will overtake sowing. The mountains will flow with sweetness, and all the hills will delight in it.

I will bring back the captives of my people Israel. They will rebuild the ruined cities and live in them. They will plant vineyards and drink their wine, and they will plant gardens and eat their fruit.
I will plant them in their own land, and they will never again be uprooted from the land I have given them, says the Lord your God.
